elements.title: TOTAL EXTERNAL DEBT STOCK, 2025
elements.description: The headline indicator shows total external debt stock in 2025. It is accompanied by a downward arrow and the change from 2024.

elements.label: Figure 1
elements.title: Total external debt, 2015–25
elements.description: The line shows total external debt from 2015 to 2025. It rises sharply in the earlier part of the period and then falls to 1,787 in 2025, below the 2015 value of 2,771.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 2
elements.title: External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations
elements.description: The stacked bars break down 2025 external debt into public and publicly guaranteed and short-term debt, then divide public and publicly guaranteed debt into multilateral and bilateral creditors. Multilateral debt exceeds bilateral debt; among the detailed creditor categories, other multilateral is largest and Kuwait is smallest.
elements.notes: Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 3
elements.title: Debt ratios, 2015–25
legend: 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries (shaded band)
elements.description: Four small line charts show external debt and debt service relative to exports and GNI from 2015 to 2025. Both debt-service ratios have a pronounced mid-period spike, while the external-debt ratios decline toward the end. In 2025, external debt / exports is the highest displayed ratio and debt service / GNI is the lowest.
elements.notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.

elements.label: Figure 4
elements.title: Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025
elements.description: Two side-by-side boxes are labeled Official creditors and Private creditors. Each lists Maturity, Grace period and Interest rate, all shown as '..'; there are no data values because the country had no new commitments in 2025.
elements.notes: Note: Figure 4 shows no data values for official or private creditors because the country did not have new commitments in 2025. Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
